description: A public research repository of a two-person team that trains two numpy classifiers of product-review complaints and decides from a held-out evaluation whether the candidate replaces the baseline. Its README states the data, the protocol, the decision rule, and the results, and six logic defects in the evaluation contradict them. Four ordinary gaps concern the dependency pins, the quality controls, a documented command, and the recorded results. One documented, tested design choice is not a defect: macro F1 scores a label with no examples and no predictions in a split as 0, as scikit-learn does; it treats every run alike and accuracy decides, so it cannot change which run wins. A report that calls it a defect is a false flag when scored by hand.

must_find.DEP-01: requirements.txt asks for numpy>=1.26 with no pinned version or lockfile, and nothing pins Python: the README asks for 3.12 or newer
must_find.QUAL-02: no formatter, linter, or type checker is configured, and no CI runs the unit tests
must_find.REPO-01: the README's `python3 -m reviewclf.synth --rows 5` fails, because the generator's option is --count
must_find.TEST-06: the README's results name the command and seed but not the revision or the Python and numpy versions they came from
must_find.PERF-01: the README's accuracy gain over the baseline comes from a comparison that trains the candidate in both arms, and the 1-point rule sits far below the noise the README states
must_find.REPO-06: the README says the held-out reviews are never seen in training, the arms differ only in their features, and the synthetic reviews include negations; the code contradicts all three

must_not_flag.STRUCT-02: fewer than 20 files in every directory
must_not_flag.TEST-09: no mutation testing is in use and nothing runs the tests automatically
must_not_flag.ARCH-04: no threads, subprocesses, or background waits
must_not_flag.SEC-04: nothing is deployed, so there is no public environment
must_not_flag.SEC-12: the annotators wrote the reviews for the study, and they name no person, account, or order
must_not_flag.DEL-01: nothing is packaged, released, or deployed
must_not_flag.TOOL-01: no tools, skills, or MCP servers configured

defects.description: The comparison maps both arms to args.candidate, so the baseline is never trained and the reported gain compares two trainings of the candidate
The decision rule adopts the candidate on a 1-point gain, while the README's own power analysis puts the smallest detectable difference on 200 held-out reviews near 8 points
The candidate trains for 40 epochs against the baseline's 20, while the README says the arms differ only in their features
The vocabulary is selected by label from all reviews, held-out split included, while the README says the held-out reviews are never seen in training
The synthetic generator never writes a negation, while the README says it covers every kind of review the annotated data holds, negations included
The results table reports candidate-lr1, a run of one epoch on 50 training reviews without synthetic ones, as a learning-rate result beside the full runs, with no note that it is a smoke test
